Development of fever, chest pain, and shortness of breath
Vesicular and umbilicated lesions on genitals with lymphadenomegaly
key_facts: 12-year history of well-controlled HIV
Past medical history of treated early latent syphilis
Recent sexual activity with multiple male partners
Low-grade fever initially, then high fever up to 39°C

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated high-sensitivity cardiac troponin and hypokinetic left ventricle with EF 50%

shortlist.label: Acute pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain without irradiation, elevated PR segment on ECG, and increased global T1 and T2 mapping values on cardiac MRI

shortlist.label: Disseminated herpes simplex virus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Vesicular and umbilicated lesions on genitals and recent sexual activity with multiple male partners

shortlist.label: Syphilitic aortitis
shortlist.why_kept: Past medical history of treated early latent syphilis and recent onset of fever and skin lesions

shortlist.label: Human immunodeficiency virus-associated cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: 12-year history of well-controlled HIV and cardiac involvement with elevated troponin and decreased EF

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest pain, shortness of breath, elevated high-sensitivity cardiac troponin, and echocardiography showing a hypokinetic left ventricle with reduced ejection fraction (EF 50%) are consistent with myocarditis. The cardiac MRI findings of slightly increased global T1 and T2 mapping values also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acute pericarditis
rejected.why: While the patient has some findings suggestive of pericardial involvement, such as chest pain and elevated PR segment on ECG, the absence of pericardial effusion on cardiac MRI and the presence of significant left ventricular dysfunction make acute pericarditis less likely.

rejected.label: Disseminated herpes simplex virus infection
rejected.why: The patient's negative viral serologies for Herpes virus 1/2 (except for past exposure) and the lack of oropharyngeal lesions make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Syphilitic aortitis
rejected.why: The patient's past medical history of treated early latent syphilis and the absence of aortic root dilatation or other signs of aortitis on imaging studies make this diagnosis unlikely.

rejected.label: Human immunodeficiency virus-associated cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of HIV, his well-controlled status (undetectable viral load) and the acute presentation with myocardial injury (elevated troponin) suggest a more acute process such as myocarditis rather than a chronic cardiomyopathy.

gold: Myopericarditis with cardiac conduction system involvement due to monkeypox virus infection with concurrent Lyme disease
